defects: Hypothesis compares m against Cardinal.toNat κ₁/κ₂ (i.e. m ≤ toNat κ) using Nat's ≤, whereas gold compares n against the cardinals themselves (n ≤ c, n ≤ d) using Cardinal's ≤, before truncation

This changes the mathematical content: in gold, 'n ≤ c' can hold for all n when c is infinite, so the hypothesis meaningfully constrains behavior of the raw cardinals; in produced, since toNat already collapses infinite cardinals to a fixed natural number, the hypothesis is just comparing two already-known naturals, making the theorem trivial (taking m = toNat κ₁ and m = toNat κ₂ immediately yields the conclusion) and losing the intended semantics of the original theorem
κ₁, κ₂ are both restricted to the same universe (Cardinal, no universe polymorphism), whereas gold allows c : Cardinal.{u}, d : Cardinal.{v} in different universes
